 Honourable Sri Justice Sambasiva Rao Naidu

sentences.text: Judgment :
This Civil Miscellaneous Appeal has been filed by the appellant, who is claimant in M.V.O.P. No.273 of 2015 on the file of II Additional District Judge, Nallakunta.

The appellant has filed this appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act assailing the award of the Court below dated 08-07-2020 by which the Court below granted a sum of Rs.4,00,000/- as compensation to the appellant herein on the ground that no adequate compensation was awarded to the appellant, thereby seeking enhancement of the compensation.

2. In fact, the appellant has filed M.V.O.P.No.273 of 2015 seeking an amount of Rs.4,00,000/-
towards compensation on account of injuries caused to him in a road traffic accident and the Tribunal awarded the said amount.
However, the appellant had filed the present appeal for additional sum of Rs.4,00,000/-.
The present appeal is filed on the following grounds.
3. The Judgment and Decree dated 08-07-2020 in M.V.O.P.No.273 of 2015 is contrary to law.

The Court below having considered the amputation of right leg of the appellant SSRN,J herein as 100%
functional disability

and it resulted loss of earning @ 100%, and having calculated an amount of Rs.5,94,000/- as compensation for disability, future earning for loss of conjugal happiness, the Court below restricted the compensation to Rs.4,00,000/- because the petition was filed for only for a sum of Rs.4,00,000/-.
The appellant has claimed that the Court below committed an error in considering the income of the injured as Rs.4,500/- per month and it ought to have calculated the same as Rs.6,000/- per month.
The Court below awarded meager amount of Rs.73,800/- under the head of future prospects and as per the Judgment of the Apex Court, future prospects to be awarded on the basis of income.
The appellant being aged about 55 years with good health and by doing cloth business as well as coolie, he was earning Rs.6,000/- per month.
Therefore, an additional amount of 15% should have been added as future prospects.

4. The appellant further claimed that the Court below failed to consider the Motor Vehicles Act as a beneficial and welfare legislation, thereby, it ought to have awarded more amount of compensation under various heads and claimed that he is entitled to an additional amount of Rs.4,00,000/- under various heads.

5. As per the petition filed by the appellant herein, vide M.V.O.P. No.273 of 2015, it was alleged that on 13-04-2015, the SSRN,J appellant and his daughter were proceeding from Nallabavi towards Vijaya Laxmi Hospital on a Mopid bearing No.AP-24-AM- 4060 and when they reached Sreedevi Bar, at about 12.45 in the noon, the first respondent who was a rider of motorcycle bearing No.AP-24-AH-0971, drove the motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the Scooty of the appellant, thereby he suffered injuries and he was immediately shifted to Ramesh Orthopedic Manda Sree Ramulu vs Vangara Pradeep Kumar on 16 June, 2023

Hospital, Suryapet, for first-aid and later shifted to Area hospital, Suryapet, where the right leg of the petitioner was amputated below the knee.
The appellant obtained follow up treatment in private hospitals.
6. The appellant has claimed that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the first respondent.
A case was registered against him.
According to the appellant, he was aged about 55 years at the time of accident, he was a coolie by profession and earning Rs.6,000/- per month.
Due to the amputation of the right leg, he suffered both physical and mental sufferance and his income was adversely affected, thereby he prayed for compensation of Rs.4,00,000/-.
Out of the three respondents shown in the petition, respondent No.2-owner of the motorcycle remained ex parte.
SSRN,J 7.
Respondents No.1 and 3 i.e., Insurance Company contested the matter.
According to the counter filed by the first respondent, it was claimed that he has got a valid driving license.
The motorbike was insured with the third respondent under a valid insurance policy.
Therefore, even if any compensation has to be paid, it must be paid by the third respondent.
Whereas, respondent No.3 filed a separate counter and disputed the material averments of the petition.
The Tribunal below framed three issues.
During inquiry, the appellant herein was examined as PW.1.
Two more witnesses were examined on his behalf.
Exs. A1
to A6 are marked by the appellant.

The respondents did not examine any witness but respondent No.3 has marked copy of the insurance policy under which the bike was insured as Ex.B1.
8.

The Tribunal having considered the oral and documentary evidence and also arguments of both parties, came to the conclusion that the appellant herein is able to prove his claim and entitled to compensation of Rs.5,94,000/-.
However, restricted the compensation to Rs.4,00,000/- in view of the total claim filed by the appellant before the Tribunal was only for Rs.4,00,000/-.
SSRN,J 9.
Even though, notices were directed to the respondents, and in spite of the service, none have appeared on behalf of respondents.

10. Heard learned counsel for the appellant.
11.

Now the point for consideration is:
Whether the appellant herein is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.4,00,000/-
in addition to the amount already awarded by the Tribunal?

If so, from whom?
12.

The appellant herein having filed a petition vide M.V.O.P.No.273 of 2015 before the trial Court/Tribunal seeking compensation for the injuries caused to him in a road traffic accident, filed the present appeal for enhancement of the compensation amount based on the observations made Manda Sree Ramulu vs Vangara Pradeep Kumar on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117350075/
2 by the learned Chairman MACT/Tribunal while awarding a sum of Rs.4,00,000/- together with costs and interest.

sentences.text: 13. As per the petition filed before the Tribunal, the appellant herein sought for a sum of Rs.4,00,000/- under various heads.
However, the appellant after filing the present appeal, filed IA.No.2 of 2021 and sought for enhancement of compensation.
The said interlocutory application was allowed on 10-03-2023.
As per the undisputed facts of the case, the appellant suffered grievous injury in the road traffic accident that took place on 13-04-2015.
In view of the accident, his right leg was amputated SSRN,J below knee.
The age of the appellant is shown as 55 years in the petition filed before the Tribunal.

Therefore, as rightly observed by the Tribunal, though the disability is shown as 60% in view of amputation of right leg below knee, it shall be treated as 100% functional disability, as the appellant cannot attend any work without the assistance of another person.

14. While filing the claim petition, the petitioner sought for a sum of Rs.4,00,000/- which includes a sum of Rs.5,000/- towards partial loss of earnings, Rs.10,000/- towards transportation charges towards hospital, Rs.50,000/- towards medical expenses, Rs.60,000/- towards compensation for pain and sufferance, Rs.15,000/- towards loss of earnings during the period of treatment and to Rs.2,60,000/- for disability.
According to the evidence of the appellant and other record, the Tribunal assessed the income of the injured as Rs.4,500/- per month.
Being an able bodied person definitely he could have earned Rs.150/- per day even by attending any coolie work.

In such a case,
in view of the age of the appellant as 55 years following the Judgment in 'Sarla Verma & Ors vs.
Delhi Transport Corporation'1, the appropriate multiplier is M-11, as such, he is entitled to 2009 (3)
ALD 83 (SC) SSRN,J Rs.5,94,000/-.

sentences.text: The Tribunal having come to such a conclusion, restricted the compensation amount to the maximum amount that was claimed in the petition filed before it.
The Tribunal ought to have awarded compensation for which the appellant is entitled by directing him to pay the deficit Court fees.

In the Judgment between 'Surekha and Ors vs. Santhosh and Ors'2,
wherein, the Hon'ble Apex Court was pleased to observe that "It is well settled in the matter of insurance claim compensation in reference to the motor accident, the Court should not take hyper technical approach and ensure that just compensation is awarded to the effected person or the claimants", and while observing soon, the Hon'ble Apex Courts modified the order passed by the High Court.

sentences.text: 15. In the case on hand, the appellant who was aged about 55 years at the time of accident suffered a grievous injury in the above referred accident and lost his right leg below the knee due to which he became permanently disabled to attend other work.

A part from mental agony and physical strain,
he need to depend upon another person for attending his own necessities.
The Tribunal while assessing the income of the appellant as Rs.4,500/- per month i.e., @ Rs.150 per day arrived a sum of Rs.5,94,000/- as compensation for disability, future earnings etc.,
However, since the claim petition was filed for a sum of (2020) SCC online SC 1312 SSRN,J Rs.2,60,000/-, restricted the amount to Rs.4,00,000/- under all the heads.

In view of the above calculations, the appellant herein is entitled to Rs.5,94,000/- as loss of earnings and compensation for the disability, apart from the same, he is also entitled to claim transport charges, medical expenses, compensation for pain and suffering.

The Tribunal having considered the oral and documentary evidence awarded a sum of Rs.5,000/- towards transport charges, Rs.46,200/- towards medical expenses and Rs.15,000/-
Manda Sree Ramulu vs Vangara Pradeep Kumar on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117350075/
3 towards compensation for pain and suffering.

sentences.text: The above said amounts are appropriate under the above heads.

Therefore, the appellant is entitled to the following amounts :
 Transport charges - 5,000/-
 Medical expenses - 46,200/-
 Pain and suffering - 15,000/-
 Permanent disability - 5,94,000/-
 and loss of future earnings _________  Total - 6,60,200/-
 _________  16.
The appellant was already awarded a sum of Rs.4,00,000/-.
Therefore, he is entitled to another sum of Rs.2,60,200/- subject to his payment of deficit Court fees.
He is entitled to recover the costs of the petition and also the interest @ SSRN,J 7% per annum from the date of petition till the entire amount is paid by the respondent.
Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed.
17. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed by granting an amount of Rs.2,60,200/-.
Consequently, Miscellaneous applications if any, are closed.
No costs.
__________ JUSTICE SAMBASIVA RAO NAIDU Date: 16.06.2023
